title: Sigarillas Winged Bean: Characteristics
metaDescription: Sigarillas winged bean: the winged bean variety, with its traits, ratings and where it grows best in the Philippines. Compare it with others.
excerpt: Sigarillas winged bean is a garden packet (type not stated) winged bean variety, also sold or known as Beans Winged Sigarillas or Ramgo sigarilyas. It is not a registered variety, so the facts here come from its seller and farm sources. It comes from Ramgo.

heroImage.alt: A farmer watering vegetable beds in Pulilan, Bulacan, the kind of farm where Sigarillas winged bean is grown

blocks.text: If you came here looking for Beans Winged Sigarillas or Ramgo sigarilyas, this is the same winged bean. The facts below come from its seller and from farm sources, each one listed at the end. Compare it with the others in our [winged bean variety finder](/crop-varieties), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for legumes](/land-preparation/legume-land-preparation).
Key facts about Sigarillas winged bean

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

Days to harvest, by the seller's count: 75 to 90 days after sowing. Yield, by the seller's count: potential 15 to 20 t/ha (seller). No trial on record checks these figures yet, so treat them as the seller's own and compare with farms near you before you plan a season around it.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit winged bean fields most often: [Cercospora leaf spot](/diseases/cercospora-leaf-spot), [powdery mildew](/diseases/powdery-mildew), [legume pod borer](/pests/legume-pod-borer), [root knot nematode](/diseases/root-knot-nematode). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Days to harvest:** 75 to 90 days after sowing.
**Fruit:** Green pods ready to pick 15 to 20 days after flowering.
Picking every two days stretches the harvest.
Guide gives a mean monthly temperature of 23 to 29 C.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: sold as a Ramgo garden seed packet. These are the seller's own figures, from its own trials. So plant a small area first, and compare it with your usual winged bean on the same ground.
Where and when to plant Sigarillas winged bean

Sigarilyas needs short days to flower well, so plant it in the second half of the year. Pick young, tender pods. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng gulay](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-gulay).

items: Buy sealed packs or tagged sacks from an accredited dealer, and check the packing date and germination rate.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Try it on a small area first, beside the variety you usually plant, before you switch the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is Beans Winged Sigarillas the same as Sigarillas?
items.a: Yes. Beans Winged Sigarillas is another name for Sigarillas. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Sigarillas?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
